Play in three minutes — no explanation needed

Audit Quest turns tonight's lecture into eight missions. Each mission gives you a real problem first, lets you take it apart, then shows the rule, the slides, the cards and a short check. Watch the animations below: they were recorded in the real game.

1Put the game file 420-D04-AB_Day09_Game_Audit-Quest_CYB-01_Fall-2026.html and this guide in the same folder.
2Double-click the game file. It opens in your browser and works without Internet (videos and links need Internet).
3Click “Start the quest →” and follow the pulsing circle. About 10 minutes per mission.
▶ Open the game
Step 1

Start the game and read the map

Open the game file in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari. The home screen explains the five stages; “Start the quest →” opens the map.

  • The pulsing circle is the next mission; you may also open any other circle.
  • The top bar shows your level, your XP and your badges.
  • Map, Library and Guide stay one click away; ↺ erases your progress on this computer.
💡 Play the missions in order the first time: each one prepares the next.
Step 2

Stage 1 — the problem

Every mission starts with a real situation from the Érable Cycles assessment. You answer before you learn — with your instinct.

  • Read the story, then click the answer you would give.
  • Every option then explains itself: green is right, red is not.
  • A right first guess gives +10 XP; a wrong one costs nothing.
💡 A wrong first guess is normal — the next stage shows why.
Step 3

Stage 2 — take it apart

The problem is cut into pieces. You sort each piece into the right box, so the rule behind the problem becomes visible.

  • Click a piece, then click a box — or drag the piece.
  • A wrong box shakes and tells you what to look for; try again.
  • Each piece placed right the first time gives +5 XP.
💡 Ask yourself: what does this piece prove, or what does it concern?
Step 4

Stage 3 — the principle

The rules that the pieces have in common, with the slides of that part of the lecture, the short videos, the abbreviations and the official sources.

  • Read the numbered rules: they are the slide messages of the lesson.
  • Click a slide to enlarge it with its note; ◀ ▶ or the arrow keys change slides, Esc closes.
  • “I have it — flash-cards →” gives +10 XP.
💡 Videos open on YouTube in a new tab; each one is 15 minutes or less.
Step 5

Stage 4 — flash-cards

Say the answer aloud, then click the card to see the back.

  • Click the card (or press Enter) to flip it.
  • ✓ I knew it gives +2 XP; ↺ Review again puts the card back at the end.
  • When every card is known, the check starts by itself.
💡 Be honest with “I knew it”: the cards come back until you know them.
Step 6

Stage 5 — the check

Questions one at a time, like the Final Exam. A question with several answers shows the number expected in brackets, for example (3).

  • One-answer question: click your answer.
  • Several answers: select them all, then “Check my answer”.
  • “Need a hint? 💡” gives a clue; every option explains why it is right or wrong. Each right answer gives +10 XP.
💡 Read the explanations of the wrong options — that is where exam traps hide.
Step 7

Badges, stars and levels

Finishing a mission gives its badge and +20 XP. Stars come from the check: 3 stars at 80 % or more, 2 stars at 50 %.

  • Finished missions turn gold on the map, with their best stars.
  • Replay any mission to improve your stars.
  • Levels: Trainee → Junior auditor (120 XP) → Auditor (300) → Senior auditor (520) → Lead auditor (760).
💡 Your progress stays in this browser on this computer; a private window does not keep it.
Step 8

The Library

Everything in one place: all 55 slides with their notes, the videos, the searchable list of abbreviations and the official links.

  • Slides & notes: click any slide to enlarge it.
  • Abbreviations: type a letter or a word to filter the list.
  • Official links: each link has a VirusTotal check button.
💡 Use the Library the evening before the Final Exam.

Questions students ask

Where is my progress saved?

In your browser, on this computer only (local storage). Nothing is sent anywhere. A private window, another browser or another computer starts from zero. The ↺ button in the top bar erases your progress.

Is the game graded?

No. It is formative practice. It uses practice data only: no graded Lab 3 Part C result appears in it.

Can I replay a mission?

Yes, as often as you want. XP is given once per action, and your best stars are kept.

The “Guide” button does not open this page.

Keep the game file and this guide file in the same folder, with their original names.

Can I use the keyboard?

Yes: Tab moves between buttons, Enter activates them, Enter flips a card, and in the slide viewer ◀ ▶ (arrow keys) change slides and Esc closes.

A video or a link does not open.

Videos and official links need Internet. Before you trust any link, use its VirusTotal check button (Legal Notice 14.2).
